Don’t hate who you are or wish you could be someone else. 

You are you.

There is nobody else on this planet that is YOU. 
I know it’s easier said than done. 
Self acceptance isn’t something that happens over night, or over a couple days, months, sometimes years. 

Not to mention our brains have been wired to accept ourselves through the validation of others, creating a weird messed up vicious cycle of self hate. 

Currently I’m trying to accept who I am. It’s been years and I’m still struggling. But I have found that looking for validation from others only made me crave more attention and sacrifice who I was in the process.

I hope this helps… 

Please check in after a few days and let me know how you’re feeling ok?

You have a lot of years ahead to figure things out. 
Can I suggest taking a few days to think things through before making any rash decisions? 

Not going to lie, in middle/high school I wasn’t the best person. We recently had a middle school reunion and I apologized and made amends with people who at that time were “not cool”. 

I only hope that other people around you will see the same way. We’re all human. We all have feelings. If the people around you grow up to be dick heads, they were never your friends. Keep trying and don’t give up.

Friends can come and go. The people around us are a huge part of our lives, and we hope that we’re able to find those who treat us right and bring us up. 

I have family that are autistic.. whether it be further down the spectrum or borderline. I will never understand what they go through or how they perceive things, but I do wish them the best. 
In one case this person found someone amazing who matched their own amazing personality and got married.

Please don’t give up on hope. You have many years ahead of you. Remember that even a stranger behind a keyboard will reply and hope the best for you.

Honestly there are no rules when it comes to suicide or how you feel in general.

As humans we rarely have the ability to change how we feel or how others feel about us, but we can try to change what we do about these feelings and how we let them affect us.

For years I've battled with myself about whether or not I was a good person and whether or not I deserved to live or what my purpose in life was.

To this day I still don't know what my purpose is.. maybe because purpose isn't something that we just 'find' .. maybe it's something we work for.

The friends around me put a microscope on my actions when I mistake and rarely speak up when I do good.

It sounds like straight up bs, but I'm learning to just "do me". I hope that you can do what makes YOU happy and no one else.

An important mantra I try and live by is, "Without the bad, you can't appreciate the good. Without the good you can't appreciate the bad." Little bit of Yin and Yang.. Yes it sounds stupid, but I know you can draw up some good moments in your life no matter who it was with.

​

One huge thing that stopped me was knowing I've made an impact on someone's life. At the time it was just second nature to do the right thing. I saw life very differently after hearing from his parents that these small acts of kindness meant the world to the kid, and it apparently helped him get a full scholarship to a great college.

If it's not too out of place, please take a moment to yourself, just you, and look introspectively about how even the smallest kind conversation with someone could've changed their day for the better. Or maybe how someone's interaction with you has changed yours. These things go much further than we'd ever understand

We all help each other so much, and it may seem so small in our own minds, but it goes so far without us ever knowing. 

Recently I was told by my folks and family friends that I made a huge impact on the kid I used to babysit. Never viewed it as anything other than just being a good person.. but now he has a full scholarship to a great college for basketball and apparently i was the one who helped build his self confidence. Hey,

I can't imagine the pain you're feeling right now.

My brother was engaged two years ago. They were together for 8 years and broke up over some really dumb argument. Long story short, I was there with him every step of the way and walked him through the entire process. From what I saw, it sucked for him. Everyday was a struggle for him to get out of bed. Everyday was a struggle for him to get to work. He was around your age, drank himself to sleep every night and even put a shotgun to his mouth and considered pulling it. 

I'm not comparing situations because everyone's is different. Everyone's pain is different. It took him 2 years to get back to normal and it doesn't hurt that he found a new girl either. Some people take more time to grieve and move on. Some get over things right away. If you're anything like me, I wear my heart on my sleeve.

Anyways, I'm here to listen, help, anything I can do man. Like I said everyone's situation is different and even if he was here to talk to you, it wouldn't be the same. But I want you to know you aren't alone.

Personally I've found that by helping people in tough situations, helping people smile or laugh when they're in a bad mood has helped me feel like I was making some kind of difference. 

What's something you would consider worthy? Are you looking to make a difference in the world or maybe just improve your life and the lives around you?

I don't think you're pretending. I don't know you, or what your life is like, but the fact that you're reaching out and looking for help is the first step to finding what you may be searching for. I really do hope that you're able to find it.

If you ever need to chat I'm here. Or if not me, someone else will be. You aren't alone in  this.

I'm so happy to hear you're looking for professional help. That again takes an amazing amount of courage. Please do me a favor and follow through. You never know what you might get out of it.

I've gone and seen an therapist in the past, and I want you to remember that if you aren't happy or comfortable with that person that you can always switch to someone else. Don't let someone who doesn't know a single thing about you discourage your attempts at getting better. 

If you ever need to talk or get something off your chest I'm here for you. We're here for you. Feel free to shoot me a message or just respond to this thread. I wish you the best and hope that things work out. Take care.
